clips.send: Common mix-up: Colds and flu are caused by viruses, so antibiotics do not help. Overusing antibiotics also helps resistant bacteria spread.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Colds and flu are caused by viruses, so antibiotics do not help. Overusing antibiotics also helps resistant bacteria spread.

clips.send: Food vacuole. Where food is digested. Engulfed food (bacteria, algae) is trapped in a food vacuole. Enzymes digest it, and nutrients pass into the cytoplasm. Food vacuole equals a tiny stomach.
clips.text: Food vacuole. Where food is digested. Engulfed food (bacteria, algae) is trapped in a food vacuole.. Enzymes digest it, and nutrients pass into the cytoplasm.. Food vacuole = a tiny stomach.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Paramecia are not animals, even though they swim and eat. They are single-celled protists.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Paramecia are not animals, even though they swim and eat. They are single-celled protists.

clips.send: Ribosomes. Make proteins. Thousands of tiny ribosomes build the proteins the cell needs. Some antibiotics work by jamming bacterial ribosomes, which differ from ours. Ribosomes equals protein factories, found in every cell.
clips.text: Ribosomes. Make proteins. Thousands of tiny ribosomes build the proteins the cell needs.. Some antibiotics work by jamming bacterial ribosomes, which differ from ours.. Ribosomes = protein factories, found in every cell.

clips.send: Nuclei. One large and one small nucleus. A paramecium has a large macronucleus that runs daily life and a small micronucleus used in reproduction. It usually reproduces by splitting in two. Macro equals big, micro equals small.
clips.text: Nuclei. One large and one small nucleus. A paramecium has a large macronucleus that runs daily life and a small micronucleus used in reproduction.. It usually reproduces by splitting in two.. Macro = big, micro = small.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Bacteria are cells, but much simpler and about 10 times smaller than your body cells.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Bacteria are cells, but much simpler and about 10 times smaller than your body cells.

clips.send: Common mix-up: Mushrooms are not plants: no chlorophyll, no photosynthesis, and chitin cell walls.
clips.text: Common mix-up: Mushrooms are not plants: no chlorophyll, no photosynthesis, and chitin cell walls.

clips.send: Cell wall and membrane. Protects the cell and controls what enters. A tough cell wall keeps the bacterium’s shape; the membrane just inside controls what goes in and out. Bacteria come in three main shapes: rods (bacilli), spheres (cocci) and spirals (spirilla). There is NO nucleus inside: bacteria are prokaryotes. Bacteria shapes: rod, ball, spiral equals bacillus, coccus, spirillum.

Bacteria shapes: rod, ball, spiral = bacillus, coccus, spirillum.

clips.send: Capsid (protein coat). A protein shell that protects the genes. The head is a 20-sided protein shell called a capsid. A virus has no cytoplasm, no ribosomes and no cell membrane: it is not a cell. Viruses are about 10–100 times smaller than bacteria. Virus equals genes in a protein box.
clips.text: Capsid (protein coat). A protein shell that protects the genes. The head is a 20-sided protein shell called a capsid.. A virus has no cytoplasm, no ribosomes and no cell membrane: it is not a cell.. Viruses are about 10–100 times smaller than bacteria.. Virus = genes in a protein box.

clips.send: Cap. Shelters the spore-making gills. The mushroom is only the fruiting body: the part that makes spores. Fungi cannot make food; they absorb it, often as decomposers. Some mushrooms are deadly poisonous: never eat wild mushrooms. Mushroom equals the “apple”; hyphae equals the “tree”.

clips.send: Oral groove. A funnel that collects food. Food (mostly bacteria) is swept down the oral groove into the cell. There it is packed into food vacuoles for digestion. Oral groove equals mouth area.
clips.text: Oral groove. A funnel that collects food. Food (mostly bacteria) is swept down the oral groove into the cell.. There it is packed into food vacuoles for digestion.. Oral groove = mouth area.

clips.send: Pili. Tiny hairs for sticking. Short hair-like pili help bacteria stick to surfaces, like your teeth or throat. Some pili let bacteria pass DNA to each other. Pili equals Velcro hooks.
clips.text: Pili. Tiny hairs for sticking. Short hair-like pili help bacteria stick to surfaces, like your teeth or throat.. Some pili let bacteria pass DNA to each other.. Pili = Velcro hooks.

clips.send: Pseudopods. “False feet” for moving and eating. The amoeba pushes out bulges of cytoplasm called pseudopods (“false feet”). It crawls by flowing into them, and wraps them around food to engulf it. Amoebas live in ponds and moist soil. Amoeba equals a shape-shifting blob.
clips.text: Pseudopods. “False feet” for moving and eating. The amoeba pushes out bulges of cytoplasm called pseudopods (“false feet”).. It crawls by flowing into them, and wraps them around food to engulf it.. Amoebas live in ponds and moist soil.. Amoeba = a shape-shifting blob.

clips.send: Contractile vacuoles. Star-shaped water pumps. Two star-shaped contractile vacuoles collect and pump out extra water. Like the amoeba’s, they stop the cell from bursting in fresh water. Stars that pump water.
clips.text: Contractile vacuoles. Star-shaped water pumps. Two star-shaped contractile vacuoles collect and pump out extra water.. Like the amoeba’s, they stop the cell from bursting in fresh water.. Stars that pump water.

clips.send: Nucleus. Control center with the DNA. Protists are eukaryotes: their DNA is inside a nucleus. An amoeba reproduces by splitting in two. Eu-karyote equals “true nucleus”.
clips.text: Nucleus. Control center with the DNA. Protists are eukaryotes: their DNA is inside a nucleus.. An amoeba reproduces by splitting in two.. Eu-karyote = “true nucleus”.

clips.send: Hyphae (mycelium). Thread network that absorbs food. Hyphae are thin threads that spread through soil or food; the whole network is the mycelium. They release digestive enzymes and absorb the nutrients. Molds and yeast are fungi too. Yeast is single-celled. Hyphae equals the fungus’s underground internet.

clips.send: Cilia. Thousands of tiny beating hairs. Cilia beat in waves, like oars, to move the paramecium quickly. They also sweep food into the oral groove. Cilia equals many tiny oars; flagellum equals one big propeller.
clips.text: Cilia. Thousands of tiny beating hairs. Cilia beat in waves, like oars, to move the paramecium quickly.. They also sweep food into the oral groove.. Cilia = many tiny oars; flagellum = one big propeller.

clips.send: Flagellum. A spinning tail for swimming. The flagellum spins like a propeller, pushing the bacterium through liquid. Some bacteria have one flagellum, others many, some none. Flagellum equals motor-driven propeller.
clips.text: Flagellum. A spinning tail for swimming. The flagellum spins like a propeller, pushing the bacterium through liquid.. Some bacteria have one flagellum, others many, some none.. Flagellum = motor-driven propeller.

clips.send: DNA (nucleoid). One loop of DNA floating in the cytoplasm. The DNA is a single circular chromosome, bunched in an area called the nucleoid. It is not wrapped in a nuclear membrane. Many bacteria also carry tiny extra DNA rings called plasmids. Pro-karyote: DNA with no “house” (nucleus).

clips.send: Tail sheath. A syringe that injects the DNA. A bacteriophage (“bacteria eater”) attacks only bacteria. The tail squeezes like a syringe to push the DNA into the bacterium. Phage tail equals a tiny syringe.
clips.text: Tail sheath. A syringe that injects the DNA. A bacteriophage (“bacteria eater”) attacks only bacteria.. The tail squeezes like a syringe to push the DNA into the bacterium.. Phage tail = a tiny syringe.

clips.send: Stalk. Lifts the cap up into the air. The stalk raises the cap so spores can catch the wind. It is made of tightly packed hyphae. Everything in a mushroom is woven from hyphae.
clips.text: Stalk. Lifts the cap up into the air. The stalk raises the cap so spores can catch the wind.. It is made of tightly packed hyphae.. Everything in a mushroom is woven from hyphae.

clips.send: Genetic material. DNA or RNA instructions to make more viruses. Inside the capsid is DNA (or RNA in viruses like flu and the common cold). When injected into a host cell, it takes over the cell’s machinery. The host cell then builds hundreds of new viruses. Viruses are “hijackers”: they use the host’s factories.

clips.send: Contractile vacuole. Pumps out extra water. Fresh water keeps leaking into the cell. The contractile vacuole fills up and squeezes the water out, so the cell does not burst. Watch it pulse! Contractile vacuole equals a bilge pump.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A virus is not a tiny bacterium. It is not a cell at all and cannot grow or reproduce outside a host cell.
clips.text: Common mix-up: A virus is not a tiny bacterium. It is not a cell at all and cannot grow or reproduce outside a host cell.

clips.send: Tail fibers. Legs that find and grab the host. The tail fibers recognize and attach to the bacterium’s surface. Each virus can only infect certain host cells, like a key fitting a lock. Lock and key: the right virus for the right cell.
clips.text: Tail fibers. Legs that find and grab the host. The tail fibers recognize and attach to the bacterium’s surface.. Each virus can only infect certain host cells, like a key fitting a lock.. Lock and key: the right virus for the right cell.

clips.send: Gills and spores. Release millions of spores. Thin gills under the cap release microscopic spores that drift in the air. A spore that lands in a good place grows new hyphae. Spores are like seeds, but just one cell.
clips.text: Gills & spores. Release millions of spores. Thin gills under the cap release microscopic spores that drift in the air.. A spore that lands in a good place grows new hyphae.. Spores are like seeds, but just one cell.

clips.send: 伸缩泡。星形的排水泵。两个星形的伸缩泡收集并排出多余的水。和变形虫一样，它们防止细胞在淡水中胀破。会排水的“小星星”。

clips.send: 容易混淆：感冒和流感是病毒引起的，吃抗生素没有用。滥用抗生素还会让耐药细菌越来越多。
clips.text: 容易混淆：感冒和流感是病毒引起的，吃抗生素没有用。滥用抗生素还会让耐药细菌越来越多。

clips.send: 菌丝(菌丝体)。吸收养分的菌丝网络。菌丝是在土壤或食物中蔓延的细丝，整个网络叫做菌丝体。它们分泌消化酶，再吸收养分。霉菌和酵母菌也是真菌，酵母菌是单细胞的。菌丝 等于 真菌的“地下互联网”。
clips.text: 菌丝(菌丝体). 吸收养分的菌丝网络. 菌丝是在土壤或食物中蔓延的细丝，整个网络叫做菌丝体。. 它们分泌消化酶，再吸收养分。. 霉菌和酵母菌也是真菌，酵母菌是单细胞的。. 菌丝 = 真菌的“地下互联网”。

clips.send: 菌毛。用来附着的细毛。短小的菌毛帮助细菌粘附在物体表面，比如你的牙齿或喉咙。有些菌毛能让细菌之间传递 DNA。菌毛 等于 魔术贴上的小钩子。

clips.send: 遗传物质。制造更多病毒的 DNA 或 RNA 指令。衣壳里面是 DNA（流感、感冒等病毒则是 RNA）。注入宿主细胞后，它会接管细胞的“机器”。宿主细胞随后会制造出成百上千个新病毒。病毒是“劫持者”：利用宿主的工厂生产自己。

clips.send: 食物泡。消化食物的地方。被吞进来的食物（细菌、藻类）包在食物泡里。酶把食物消化，养分进入细胞质。食物泡 等于 小小的胃。
clips.text: 食物泡. 消化食物的地方. 被吞进来的食物（细菌、藻类）包在食物泡里。. 酶把食物消化，养分进入细胞质。. 食物泡 = 小小的胃。

clips.send: 菌盖。保护产生孢子的菌褶。蘑菇只是真菌的子实体，也就是产生孢子的部分。真菌不能制造食物，而是吸收养分，常常充当分解者。有些蘑菇有剧毒：千万不要采食野生蘑菇。蘑菇像“苹果”，菌丝才是“树”。
clips.text: 菌盖. 保护产生孢子的菌褶. 蘑菇只是真菌的子实体，也就是产生孢子的部分。. 真菌不能制造食物，而是吸收养分，常常充当分解者。. 有些蘑菇有剧毒：千万不要采食野生蘑菇。. 蘑菇像“苹果”，菌丝才是“树”。

clips.send: 核糖体。合成蛋白质。成千上万个微小的核糖体合成细胞需要的蛋白质。有些抗生素通过“卡住”细菌的核糖体起作用，因为它们和我们的核糖体不同。核糖体 等于 蛋白质工厂，所有细胞都有。
clips.text: 核糖体. 合成蛋白质. 成千上万个微小的核糖体合成细胞需要的蛋白质。. 有些抗生素通过“卡住”细菌的核糖体起作用，因为它们和我们的核糖体不同。. 核糖体 = 蛋白质工厂，所有细胞都有。

clips.send: 鞭毛。用来游动的旋转“尾巴”。鞭毛像螺旋桨一样旋转，推动细菌在液体中前进。有的细菌只有一根鞭毛，有的有很多根，有的没有。鞭毛 等于 带马达的螺旋桨。
clips.text: 鞭毛. 用来游动的旋转“尾巴”. 鞭毛像螺旋桨一样旋转，推动细菌在液体中前进。. 有的细菌只有一根鞭毛，有的有很多根，有的没有。. 鞭毛 = 带马达的螺旋桨。

clips.send: 伪足。用来运动和摄食的“假脚”。变形虫伸出细胞质形成的突起，叫做伪足（“假脚”）。它让身体流进伪足来爬行，并用伪足包围、吞噬食物。变形虫生活在池塘和潮湿的土壤中。变形虫 等于 会变形的“果冻”。

clips.send: 菌柄。把菌盖举到空中。菌柄把菌盖举高，孢子才能被风吹走。它由紧密排列的菌丝构成。蘑菇的每一部分都是由菌丝“编织”成的。
clips.text: 菌柄. 把菌盖举到空中. 菌柄把菌盖举高，孢子才能被风吹走。. 它由紧密排列的菌丝构成。. 蘑菇的每一部分都是由菌丝“编织”成的。

clips.send: 尾丝。寻找并抓住宿主的“腿”。尾丝能识别并附着在细菌表面。每种病毒只能感染特定的宿主细胞，就像钥匙只能开对应的锁。锁和钥匙：特定病毒只感染特定细胞。
clips.text: 尾丝. 寻找并抓住宿主的“腿”. 尾丝能识别并附着在细菌表面。. 每种病毒只能感染特定的宿主细胞，就像钥匙只能开对应的锁。. 锁和钥匙：特定病毒只感染特定细胞。

clips.send: 菌褶和孢子。释放数百万个孢子。菌盖下薄薄的菌褶释放出微小的孢子，随空气飘散。孢子落到合适的地方，就会长出新的菌丝。孢子像种子，但只有一个细胞。
clips.text: 菌褶和孢子. 释放数百万个孢子. 菌盖下薄薄的菌褶释放出微小的孢子，随空气飘散。. 孢子落到合适的地方，就会长出新的菌丝。. 孢子像种子，但只有一个细胞。

clips.send: 衣壳(蛋白质外壳)。保护遗传物质的蛋白质外壳。头部是一个 20 面体的蛋白质外壳，叫做衣壳。病毒没有细胞质、没有核糖体，也没有细胞膜：它不是细胞。病毒比细菌小 10到100 倍。病毒 等于 装在蛋白质盒子里的基因。
clips.text: 衣壳(蛋白质外壳). 保护遗传物质的蛋白质外壳. 头部是一个 20 面体的蛋白质外壳，叫做衣壳。. 病毒没有细胞质、没有核糖体，也没有细胞膜：它不是细胞。. 病毒比细菌小 10~100 倍。. 病毒 = 装在蛋白质盒子里的基因。

clips.send: 细胞核。一个大核和一个小核。草履虫有一个控制日常生活的大核，和一个参与繁殖的小核。它通常通过一分为二来繁殖。大核管生活，小核管繁殖。
clips.text: 细胞核. 一个大核和一个小核. 草履虫有一个控制日常生活的大核，和一个参与繁殖的小核。. 它通常通过一分为二来繁殖。. 大核管生活，小核管繁殖。

clips.send: 容易混淆：草履虫会游、会吃，但它不是动物，而是单细胞的原生生物。
clips.text: 容易混淆：草履虫会游、会吃，但它不是动物，而是单细胞的原生生物。

clips.send: 容易混淆：细菌是细胞，但比你的体细胞简单得多，也小约 10 倍。
clips.text: 容易混淆：细菌是细胞，但比你的体细胞简单得多，也小约 10 倍。

clips.send: 容易混淆：蘑菇不是植物：没有叶绿素，不进行光合作用，细胞壁含几丁质。
clips.text: 容易混淆：蘑菇不是植物：没有叶绿素，不进行光合作用，细胞壁含几丁质。

clips.send: 尾鞘。注射 DNA 的“注射器”。噬菌体（“吃细菌的”）只攻击细菌。尾鞘像注射器一样收缩，把 DNA 注入细菌。噬菌体的尾巴 等于 微型注射器。
clips.text: 尾鞘. 注射 DNA 的“注射器”. 噬菌体（“吃细菌的”）只攻击细菌。. 尾鞘像注射器一样收缩，把 DNA 注入细菌。. 噬菌体的尾巴 = 微型注射器。

clips.send: DNA(拟核)。漂浮在细胞质中的一个 DNA 环。DNA 是一条环状染色体，聚集在叫做“拟核”的区域。它没有核膜包裹。许多细菌还带有叫做“质粒”的小 DNA 环。原核生物：DNA 没有“房子”（细胞核）。
clips.text: DNA(拟核). 漂浮在细胞质中的一个 DNA 环. DNA 是一条环状染色体，聚集在叫做“拟核”的区域。. 它没有核膜包裹。. 许多细菌还带有叫做“质粒”的小 DNA 环。. 原核生物：DNA 没有“房子”（细胞核）。

clips.send: 容易混淆：病毒不是“很小的细菌”。它根本不是细胞，离开宿主细胞就不能生长或繁殖。
clips.text: 容易混淆：病毒不是“很小的细菌”。它根本不是细胞，离开宿主细胞就不能生长或繁殖。

clips.send: 细胞壁和细胞膜。保护细胞，控制物质进出。坚韧的细胞壁维持细菌的形状；内侧的细胞膜控制物质进出。细菌主要有三种形状：杆状（杆菌）、球状（球菌）和螺旋状（螺旋菌）。细胞里没有细胞核：细菌是原核生物。细菌三形状：杆菌、球菌、螺旋菌。
clips.text: 细胞壁和细胞膜. 保护细胞，控制物质进出. 坚韧的细胞壁维持细菌的形状；内侧的细胞膜控制物质进出。. 细菌主要有三种形状：杆状（杆菌）、球状（球菌）和螺旋状（螺旋菌）。. 细胞里没有细胞核：细菌是原核生物。. 细菌三形状：杆菌、球菌、螺旋菌。

clips.send: 纤毛。成千上万根摆动的细毛。纤毛像船桨一样成波浪状摆动，让草履虫快速游动。它们还把食物扫进口沟。纤毛 等于 很多小船桨；鞭毛 等于 一个大螺旋桨。

clips.send: 细胞核。储存 DNA 的控制中心。原生生物是真核生物：DNA 位于细胞核内。变形虫通过一分为二来繁殖。真核生物 等于 有真正的细胞核。

clips.send: 伸缩泡。排出多余的水。淡水会不断渗入细胞。伸缩泡把水收集起来再挤出去，防止细胞胀破。看，它在一张一缩！伸缩泡 等于 排水泵。

clips.send: 口沟。收集食物的“漏斗”。食物（主要是细菌）被扫进口沟，进入细胞。食物在里面被包进食物泡消化。口沟 等于 嘴巴所在的地方。
